title: The Asset of the Green Zone
premise: Paloma Pemberton, a hostage negotiator haunted by the death of a hostage she couldn't save, is pulled into an international crisis when her own voiceprint unlocks a shadow server containing plans for a staged 'accident' at an upcoming summit. The server was built by her estranged father, a disgraced intelligence officer whose inheritance of secrets she never wanted. As Paloma negotiates with the attack's architect—a man who believes justice outside the law is the only kind left—she must choose between exposing her father's legacy and saving hundreds of lives. In the end, she talks the bomber down not with force but with the truth of her own failure, then dismantles her father's network, finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: Ulyana Sterling is a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to people on the worst nights of their lives before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the quiet mechanics of persuasion and the people who talk others back from the edge.

chapters.title: The Voice That Wakes the Machine
chapters.summary: Paloma Pemberton, POV. Three a.m. again, and Paloma replays the failed negotiation that cost a hostage her life. A cryptic email arrives: a server in Nairobi has unlocked itself, triggered by her voiceprint from an old recorded call. The emotional beat is dread—her past has a key to her future.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Static
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. She flies to Nairobi and, with a local fixer named Baraka, accesses the server: her father's voice, dead two years, narrating files about a plot called GREENZONE. The beat is vertigo—grief curdling into suspicion that her father's death was staged.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Filed
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV, with flashbacks to her father's cold silences. The files map an attack on the Meridian Summit disguised as an infrastructure accident. Interpol flags her access within hours. The beat is claustrophobia: she's now both investigator and suspect.

chapters.title: Baraka's Bargain
chapters.summary: Baraka, POV. The fixer reveals he was paid by Paloma's father to wait for her, holding a sealed letter and a burner phone. He's torn between the money owed to his family and the danger of the company he's keeping. The beat is divided loyalty.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. The letter is half-apology, half-instruction: 'Trust the man who asks the wrong questions.' Interpol agent Ines Rocha corners Paloma in her hotel; instead of arresting her, Rocha offers a quiet, off-book alliance. The beat is wary trust.

chapters.title: Questions in the Wrong Order
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Following the letter's riddle, she meets a retired engineer who confirms the attack: a gas main 'failure' timed to the summit's opening ceremony. The engineer is found dead hours later. The beat is the first blood—this is real and accelerating.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers
chapters.summary: New POV: Elias Voss, the attack's architect, a former negotiator Paloma's father trained. Voss believes institutions murdered his family and buried the truth; the summit's attendees are his chosen jury. The beat is chilling sympathy—we understand him.

chapters.title: Negotiation 101
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Voss contacts her directly: he unlocked her voiceprint deliberately, choosing her as his counterpart because she is her father's daughter. He offers proof of her father's murder in exchange for her silence. The beat is seduction of a deal.

chapters.title: Rocha's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines Rocha, POV. Rocha's superiors want the summit protected at any cost, including letting a scapegoat take the fall—and they've chosen Paloma. Rocha must decide whether the system she serves deserves her loyalty. The beat is institutional betrayal.

chapters.title: The Wrong Question
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. She asks Voss the 'wrong question' from the letter: not why he's doing this, but who taught him that grief justifies arithmetic. Voss falters on camera, revealing a live feed of the target site. The beat is a crack in the armor.

chapters.title: Green Zone
chapters.summary: Paloma and Baraka, POV alternating. They infiltrate the decommissioned waterworks beneath the summit district where the gas device is staged. Baraka is captured buying them time. The beat is sacrifice—the cost of the inheritance becomes personal.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Voss offers Baraka's release for Paloma's public confession that her father was the attack's true author, posthumously framing him. The beat is moral crucible: to save her friend, she must bury her father twice.

chapters.title: The Failure on the Board
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV, deep flashback. The full truth of her failed negotiation: the hostage died because Paloma followed protocol instead of her instinct—and her father had quietly rewritten the protocol to test her. The beat is devastating reframe of her guilt.

chapters.title: Two Negotiators
chapters.summary: Paloma and Voss, alternating POV. A face-to-face meeting in a neutral chapel, both trained in the same school of listening. Voss admits he wants her to stop him—he's been waiting for someone to talk him down. The beat is terrible honesty.

chapters.title: Rocha Breaks Rank
chapters.summary: Ines Rocha, POV. Rocha discovers her superiors knew about the plot months ago and let it mature to justify a security crackdown. She burns her career, feeding Paloma the device's true trigger mechanism. The beat is justice choosing sides.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Summit eve. The device arms on a timer Voss can delay but not stop remotely. Paloma must go back under the waterworks alone while Rocha runs interference above. The beat is the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Grief
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Beneath the city, Paloma negotiates not for surrender but for Voss's witness: she convinces him that a dead man's confession convicts no one, and that his testimony alive is the only justice his family will ever get. The beat is persuasion as salvation.

chapters.title: Disarm
chapters.summary: Paloma and Voss, POV. Together they defuse the device with minutes left as Rocha's team closes in. Voss surrenders to Paloma personally, not to the state. Baraka, wounded but alive, is freed. The beat is exhausted, trembling triumph.

chapters.title: The Hearing Nobody Broadcasts
chapters.summary: Ines Rocha, POV. Voss testifies in a sealed tribunal, implicating the officials who nurtured the plot. Rocha's superiors fall; her career survives in a smaller, cleaner form. The beat is justice outside the law, barely, imperfectly achieved.

chapters.title: What Paloma Keeps
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Sorting her father's effects, she finds the one honest thing he left: a recording apologizing for the protocol, for the test, for the silence. She keeps the recording and burns the rest. The beat is chosen inheritance.

chapters.title: Baraka's Village
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. She travels with Baraka to his family's home to repay the debt she owes, staying a week among people who measure wealth differently. The beat is belonging found outside the crisis, in ordinary hours.

chapters.title: Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Back home, Paloma takes a new case—a routine one, low stakes, a frightened man on a ledge—and talks him down with steady hands. That night she sleeps eight full hours. The beat is quiet, hard-won peace.
